stem: When you construct `QiskitRuntimeService()` without specifying a `channel`, which channel is used by default?

options.text: `ibm_cloud` — the channel name used by the older IBM Cloud service
`ibm_quantum` — the legacy IBM Quantum Platform channel
There is no default: `QiskitRuntimeService()` raises unless a saved account or a `channel=` argument supplies one.
`ibm_quantum_platform` is what `save_account` writes, while a bare `QiskitRuntimeService()` falls back to the `local` channel.

explanation.correct: The default channel is `ibm_quantum_platform`. Because this is almost always the appropriate channel, the docs omit it from the examples; you only pass `channel=` to override it.

distractors.A: `ibm_cloud` is a separate channel value, not the default.
distractors.C: `ibm_quantum` was the legacy channel used by the older platform; it is not the current default and this is a common out-of-date assumption.
distractors.D: `local` is a real channel for local testing (`QiskitRuntimeService(channel="local")`), but it is not the default; the default is `ibm_quantum_platform`. You get the local channel only by requesting it explicitly, so `local` is never the default.
distractors.E: There is a documented default. A bare `QiskitRuntimeService()` is the ordinary way to construct the service precisely because `channel` falls back to `ibm_quantum_platform`.
distractors.F: `local` is never a fallback — it is an explicit opt-in for local testing mode. The same default applies whether you are saving an account or constructing the service.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — gave every channel option a descriptor so the correct one is no longer the longest. | pool wave: +E (channel has no default), +F (bare constructor falls back to the local channel)
